Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the UniInsure Corporation Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to UniInsure Corporation's Second Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Underwriting Officer; Emily Wong, Chief Investment Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Operating Officer; and Karen Patel, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on UniInsure Corporation's performance for the second quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust policy retention rates across major product lines, manageable total catastrophe losses relative to gross written premium, a fortified capital position with elevated statutory surplus levels, reliable reinsurance recoveries both received and anticipated, favorable realized and unrealized gains on our investment portfolio, disciplined combined ratio performance overall and by segment, and positive expense ratio trends amid controlled commission and operating costs. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives.

Lisa Chen, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. As Mark mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included resilient policy retention, controlled catastrophe impacts, strong capital metrics, effective reinsurance support, attractive investment returns, superior combined ratio execution, and expense efficiency gains. Our combined ratio was 92.3%. Investment income for the quarter was $320 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with $18.7 billion in statutory surplus. Our expense ratio also improved to 28.5%.

Let me expand on these operational metrics that underpin our long-term value creation, starting with one of our key leading indicators: policy retention rates by major product line. Retention is the foundation of our combined ratio discipline and premium growth path, influencing our book-to-bill ratio and embedded value. For the quarter, our overall retention rate across the enterprise was 91.8%, up 130 basis points year-over-year from 90.5% and 40 basis points sequentially from the first quarter's 91.4%. This represents our 11th consecutive quarter of sequential gains, thanks to advanced pricing analytics, digital servicing enhancements, and focused loyalty initiatives.

Breaking it down by major lines with comparisons for perspective, personal lines, at 42% of in-force premium, showed auto retention at 89.7%, up 80 basis points year-over-year but stable sequentially. This held firm amid market rate pressures where rivals implemented 15-20% increases due to repair inflation and post-COVID frequency rises. Our telematics offering, UniDrive, now covers over 1.2 million policyholders and added a 2.5-point boost via safe driving discounts—our safe drivers retain at 94.2%. High-frequency areas like Florida and California saw 87.1% retention from litigation trends in hurricanes and wildfires.

Homeowners and dwellers excelled at 93.4%, up 160 basis points year-over-year and 50 basis points sequentially, powered by 68% bundling penetration that lifts retention 4-5 points over monoline. Climate-resilient underwriting through our CatIQ model trimmed wildfire exposure in California (90.2% there) while growing in the Midwest at 92.8%. This drove 8.2% renewal premium growth, outperforming peers via parametric endorsements for secondary perils.

Commercial lines, 35% of in-force premium, had small commercial P&C under $50K at 92.3%, up 210 basis points year-over-year and 60 basis points sequentially. Agent portal upgrades and QuickBooks APIs enable round-the-clock service, beating industry averages, with cross-sell into cyber boosting results. Middle market and specialty over $50K was 88.9%, up 90 basis points year-over-year but down slightly sequentially in a softening excess and surplus market. GLMs mitigate adverse selection in construction and hospitality; Europe hit 86.5% from UK floods, but Asia-Pacific acquisition added 91.2% from D&O and supply chain demand.

Life and annuity, 15% of premium, saw individual life at 95.2%, stable year-over-year and up 30 basis points sequentially, with lapses at 4.8% below benchmarks, aided by no-lapse guarantees and IUL crediting at 6.2%. We're pushing whole life in the US Southeast at 97.1% to offset variable annuity runoff.

Group and health, 8% of premium, reached 97.1% for employee benefits and stop loss, up 40 basis points, via ASO models and wearable integrations cutting claims. Midwestern self-funded groups exceed 98.3%.

Regionally, North America blended at 92.5%, Northeast leading at 94.1%; California at 88.3% from rate delays, addressed by non-renewals. Europe at 90.2% with Solvency II benefits, APAC at 93.8% on manufacturing growth.

Tech like our AI renewal optimizer—scanning 150+ variables—lifted retention 1.8 points enterprise-wide, while app chatbots cut service times 40%, raising NPS to 81. Cat bond issuances stabilized reinsurance, enabling 5-7% renewals. We're targeting 92-93% full-year with retention squads, prioritizing quality like Berkshire but with Chubb agility.

Shifting to catastrophe losses, a key volatility gauge for P&C insurers, our total cat losses were $482 million pre-tax, or 2.4% of quarterly gross written premium of $20.1 billion. This compares to $295 million or 1.6% last year on $18.4 billion GWP. Year-to-date, $1.12 billion or 2.8% of $39.8 billion GWP, up from 2.2%. Sequentially softer than Q1's $638 million due to fewer tornadoes, but up from hurricane activity.

US drove 68% or $328 million, with Hurricane Beryl at $215 million in homeowners and commercial property on the Gulf Coast—RMS models revised down 12%. Midwest storms added $113 million in auto and small commercial, exceeding 1-in-50 year expectations by 15%.

Europe 18% or $87 million from German/Polish floods; higher deductibles contained motor/SME claims. Asia-Pacific 9% or $43 million from Indian landslides on crop reinsurance, Australian wildfires at $24 million aided by pools. Other 5% or $24 million from Canadian hail and Japanese quakes, protected above $50 million by Swiss Re retro.

Excluding cats, loss ratio was 58.2% from 60.1% year-over-year. All-in accident year combined ratio 98.4%, cats adding 480 points, in our 95-100% ex-cat target. At 2.4% of GWP, above our 1.8% five-year average but below industry 2.7%.

We've upgraded to AIR Touchstone with ML for climate projections, cutting uncertainty 22%. Reduced Texas wind 15%, shifted to parametrics in Florida. 2024 reinsurance has higher towers, 40% collateralized, aggregate covers. Guide full-year cats $2.3-2.7 billion or 2.5-3.0% of $92 billion GWP, with 8-12% pricing in vulnerable lines at 105% adequacy. Piloting wildfire early warnings.

Now, on combined ratio, our gold standard for underwriting health: consolidated at 92.3%, down 180 basis points from 94.1% year-over-year and better than full-year 2023's 93.8%—10th quarter under 95%. Pure loss ratio 61.2% from 64.5%, with $145 million favorable prior-year development or 2.8 points from auto physical damage and workers' comp. Cats at $210 million or 4.1 points from Midwest/Southeast hail/wind. Expense ratio steady at 31.1%, accruing 1.2 points for Florida filings against AOB risks.

By segment: Personal lines, 57% of $2.8 billion earned premiums up 8%, at 91.5% vs. 93.2%. Auto 89.8% on $1.6 billion up 7%, telematics at 42% penetration improving selection 15%, rates up 6.2%, PYD 3.1 points. Homeowners 95.2% on $1.2 billion up 9%, ex-cat 88%, AI models enabling 12% hikes.

Commercial lines, 28% of $1.4 billion up 12%, at 93.1% vs. 96.4%. Workers' comp 92.7% from return-to-office, Schedule Rating at 35%. Middle-market 94.5%, 4.2 points PYD, ESG pricing with Verisk growing premiums 15%.

Specialty 15% of $750 million up 15%, at 90.8% vs. 91.5%. Cyber 88.2% with sub-limits despite hacks, D&O 92.1% with PYD, parametrics up 25%.

US 92.0% on 82% earned premiums, Europe 94.5%, APAC 89.2%. Underwriting 2025 uses ML for pricing, targeting sub-90% ex-cat. Optimized reinsurance to 28% ceded. Accident-year ex-cat/PYD 94.7%; full-year guide 92.5-94.0% with 4-5 cat points.

Expense ratio improved to 28.5%, down 170 basis points year-over-year from 30.2% and 40 basis points sequentially—sixth straight quarter better, trailing twelve-month at 29.1%, below 28-30% target and peers.

Commissions at 12.1%, down 20 basis points year-over-year. P&C agents at 10.8% with digital portal reducing errors 35%. Life/Health up to 18.2% offset by DTC at 22% new policies. US 11.5%, EMEA 13.8%, APAC 14.2%. Expect 11.8-12.0% with DTC to 25%, performance incentives.

Operating costs 16.4%, down 4.2% per premium or $180 million saved. Apex Digital Horizon with Guidewire automates 70% underwriting, AI triage to 45% straight-through, saving 18%. Employee costs up 6%, facilities 3%, but LAE down 12%. North America 15.9%, EMEA 17.2%, APAC 18.1%.

Pillars: scale from 7% GWP growth, tech ROI 3:1 on $400 million spend, loss ratio leverage from 95.2% combined. RPA for 80% servicing, UBI with Verizon for efficiencies. Path to sub-28%, boosting ROE 12-15%.

Capital position: statutory surplus $18.7 billion, up 12% year-over-year from $16.7 billion, 3.2% sequentially. Driven by 92.8% P&C combined, $450 million reserve releases, $620 million net investment income from higher fixed-income yields. RBC at 512%, above 450% target, top quartile. P&C 528%, L&H 485%, annuities 495%.

Five-year CAGR 10.8% vs. industry 7.2%. P&C up 14% to $12.4 billion, L&H 9% to $4.1 billion. US $15.2 billion at over 550% RBC, PML under 15%. Europe up 18% to €1.8 billion at 220% Solvency II, APAC doubled to $1.2 billion.

Renewed XoL tower saving 25%, $250 million cat bond via SPV. BlackLine/Moody's for reporting. $1.5 billion buyback ($450 million YTD), 8% dividend hike to $0.65. M&A in E&S, derisking swaps.

Reinsurance recoveries: $1.2 billion received in quarter, up 28% year-over-year, 15% sequentially; YTD $3.1 billion or 62% of gross losses. Cats 42% or $504 million—Idalia $285 million of $320 million ceded. Non-cat/large losses 35% or $420 million, $250 million PYD. Short-tail 23% or $276 million.

Expected $2.8 billion more: $1.4 billion 2023 cats, $850 million prior years, $550 million longevity. 94% recovery rate, 35% funds-withheld. Up 22% year-over-year from higher limits amid 15-25% hardening. Ceded 12-point loss ratio boost to 62.4%.

NA 65%, Europe 18%, APAC 12%. AI BF models with RMS improve forecasts 15%, $500 million cat bond. Optimizing ceding commissions to 75/25 gross-net.

Investments: $285 million contribution from $152 billion portfolio, duration 5.8 years matching liabilities. Realized net gain $312 million, up 45% QoQ—$245 million fixed-income sales ($4.2 billion trimmed corporates/munis), $45 million equities (NVIDIA/Microsoft), $22 million alts. Minimal $20 million losses. YTD $620 million toward $1.1-1.3 billion.

Unrealized $27 million gain, narrowing net loss to $2.8 billion or 1.8%. Rates rallied Treasuries $1.2 billion, corporates $650 million. Equities $180 million, HY $320 million. NA $1.8 billion, Europe $150 million, APAC/EM -$80 million.

Hedged $12 billion swaps/futures. 4.6% new money yield, 4.2% portfolio, Sharpe 1.1. Q3 realized $250-300 million. ESG $5 billion green bonds, private credit to 10%.

These elements affirm our trajectory for mid-teens EPS growth and ROE.

David Ramirez: Thank you, Lisa. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our personal and commercial lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and high-frequency auto states, and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-powered peril modeling and telematics-driven pricing.

Emily Wong: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and alternatives.

Karen Patel: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI-driven triage that accelerates straight-through processing to 45% for minor claims. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times and lower handling costs.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the drivers behind your policy retention improvements across segments?

Mark Thompson: Good morning, John. Absolutely. As Lisa detailed, our 91.8% enterprise retention reflects targeted tech like the AI optimizer and UniDrive telematics, alongside bundling and loyalty programs. In personal auto and homeowners, we're seeing outsized gains from safe driver cohorts and climate modeling, while commercial benefits from agent portals and cyber cross-sell. This positions us for sustained premium growth without sacrificing quality.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of heightened catastrophe activity on your business?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Maria. While Q2 cats at 2.4% of GWP pressured results, our ex-cat loss ratio improved to 58.2%, and reinsurance recoveries offset much of the volatility. Proactive portfolio actions like Texas non-renewals and enhanced modeling keep us within guidance, with full-year cats at 2.5-3.0%. Our combined ratio resilience underscores the underlying strength.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim: What is the expected impact of potential regulatory changes in catastrophe-prone states like Florida on your underwriting strategy?

David Ramirez: Good morning, David. We're ahead of the curve with 1.2-point accruals for filings and pruning 15% high-risk coastal books. Parametric shifts and rate adequacy at 105% via Earnix ensure discipline. Regulatory hurdles like prop-103 delays are managed through non-renewals and tech for elasticity, maintaining our sub-95% targets.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thanks. On capital, how does the $18.7 billion surplus inform your M&A and return plans?

Lisa Chen: Hi Alex. The 512% RBC gives tremendous flexibility—we've deployed $450 million in buybacks, hiked dividends 8%, and have $2-3 billion for bolt-ons in E&S. Cat bonds and reinsurance savings free up more collateral, supporting 10%+ surplus per share growth while derisking via swaps.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] That concludes our Q&A session.

Mark Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in UniInsure Corporation. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
